extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and practitioners (appellants, patent owners, third‑party requesters) participating in inter partes reexamination appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and required content for drafting an examiner's answer and related papers in inter partes reexamination appeals (form paragraphs, required explanations of rejections/findings, treatment of claims appendices, evidence listings, rebuttal briefs, and oral hearing requests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement With Statement of the Grounds of Rejection on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of the grounds of rejection contained in the [1] brief(s) is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify the brief(s) containing the correct statement (e.g., “appellant third party requester Jones” or “appellant patent owner and respondent third party requester Smith”). Follow with form paragraph 26.54.011 if there are grounds not withdrawn and not presented by an appellant for review. Follow with form paragraph 26.54.012 to list any non-appealable issues. Use form paragraph 26.54.02 where there is disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of Rejection Not on Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The following grounds of rejection have not been withdrawn by the examiner, and they have not been presented by an appellant for review. [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify each ground of rejection that has not been withdrawn and has not been presented by an appellant for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonappealable Issue in Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief presents arguments relating to [2]. This issue relates to petitionable subject matter under 37 CFR 1.181 and not to appealable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify the brief containing the petitionable issues (e.g., “appellant third party requester Jones” or “appellant patent owner”). Use this paragraph to list any non-appealable issues in the brief(s). Follow with form paragraph 26.55.011 if there are findings of patentability not withdrawn and not presented by an appellant for review. When more than one brief has a petitionable issue, use the form paragraph for each brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of Patentability Not on Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The following grounds of rejection have not been withdrawn by the examiner, and they have not been presented by an appellant for review. [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify each ground of rejection that has not been withdrawn and has not been presented by an appellant for review (used for findings of patentability not on review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disagreement With Statement of the Grounds of Rejection on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The [1] brief(s) does/do not provide a correct statement of the grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal. [2] The grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal are as follows: [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify the brief(s) containing the incorrect statement. In bracket 2, indicate the area of disagreement and the reasons for the disagreement. In bracket 3 set forth the correct statement of the grounds of rejection on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement With Statement of the Findings of Patentability on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of the findings of patentability contained in the [1] brief(s) is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify the brief(s) containing the correct statement of the findings of patentability on appeal (e.g., “appellant third party requester Jones” or “appellant patent owner”). Follow with form paragraph 26.55.01 or 26.55.02 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disagreement With Statement of the Findings of Patentability on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The [1] brief(s) does/do not provide a correct statement of the findings of patentability to be reviewed on appeal. [2] The findings of patentability to be reviewed on appeal are as follows: [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify the brief(s) containing the incorrect statement. In bracket 2, indicate the area of disagreement and reasons for the disagreement. In bracket 3, set forth the correct statement of the patentability to be reviewed on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix — Correct Copy in Appellant Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the appealed claims [1] contained in the Appendix to the appellant brief of [2] is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, identify the claims appealed found in the appellant brief. In bracket 2, identify the appellant brief containing the claims appealed (e.g., ‘‘third party requester,’’ ‘‘third party requester Smith,’’ or ‘‘patent owner’’). Use this paragraph for appellant briefs, not respondent briefs. Where more than one appellant brief exists, the examiner may choose any appellant brief that has a correct copy of the claims appealed. If a claim is correct in one appellant brief but incorrect in another, draw a diagonal line through the incorrect claim in the Appendix of the incorrect brief and annotate with date, “Incorrect,” and examiner initials (paper file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix — Substantially Correct Copy
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantially correct copy of the appealed claim(s) is contained in the Appendix of the appellant brief of [1]. Claim(s) [2] appear on pages [3] of the appendix contain minor errors. The minor errors are as follows: [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where all appellant briefs contain errors in the claim(s) but at least one appellant brief is substantially correct and contains only minor errors. In bracket 1 identify the appellant brief containing the substantially correct copy. In bracket 2 indicate the claim(s) with minor errors, in bracket 3 identify the page(s) where the substantially correct appealed claims appear, and in bracket 4 indicate the nature of the errors. For paper files, draw a diagonal line through incorrect claims in other briefs and annotate as noted above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix — Substantial Errors (Attach Correct Copy / Require Corrected Brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] contain(s) substantial errors as presented in the Appendix to all the appellant briefs. Accordingly, claim(s) [2] is/are correctly written in the Appendix to the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when all appellants fail to include a correct copy of an appealed claim or claims in the Appendix to the brief. Attach a correct copy of the claims incorrect in all appellant briefs as an Appendix to the examiner’s answer; in a paper file, draw a diagonal line through the incorrect claim in each appellant brief and place date, “Incorrect,” and examiner initials. If errors are significant, rather than use this paragraph, appellant(s) should be required to submit a corrected (amended) brief. When briefs include arguments based on incorrect versions of claims, a corrected brief should always be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Relied Upon — Examiner Listing
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is a listing of the evidence (e.g., patents, publications, official notice, and admitted prior art) relied upon by the examiner in the rejection of claims under appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the example format for each reference: Number | Name | Date. Examples provided (e.g., 2,717,847 VARIAN 9-1955; 1,345,890 MUTHER 7-1963). See MPEP § 707.05(e) for additional examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Relied Upon — Requester Listing
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is a listing of the evidence relied upon by the third party requester(s) in the proposed rejection of claims which were not made by the examiner, and are now under appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same reference format: Number | Name | Date. Examples provided; see MPEP § 707.05(e) for more examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of Rejection — General Explanation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The following ground(s) of rejection are applicable to the appealed claims. [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, explain each ground of rejection clearly and completely as set forth in paragraphs (i)-(vi) (see separate items for statutory-specific explanation requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph — Examiner's Explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the examiner’s answer shall explain why the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is not complied with, including, as appropriate, how the specification and drawings, if any, (a) do not describe the subject matter defined by each of the rejected claims, and/or (b) would not enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter defined by each of the rejected claims without undue experimentation including a consideration of the undue experimentation factors set forth in MPEP § 2164.01(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain specifically where the written description or enablement is deficient and address undue experimentation factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph — Examiner's Explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner’s answer shall explain why the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which “applicant” regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the claim language deficiencies that render the claims indefinite or not distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 — Examiner's Explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the examiner’s answer shall explain why the rejected claims are anticipated or not patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102, pointing out where all of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the art relied upon in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to exact locations in the prior art that disclose each claim limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 — Examiner's Explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner’s answer shall state the ground of rejection and point out where each of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims is found in the prior art relied on in the rejection, shall identify any difference between the rejected claims and the prior art relied on (i.e., the primary reference) and shall explain why it would have been obvious at the time the invention was made to a person of ordinary skill in the art to have modified the primary reference to arrive at the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the differences and provide a rationale for the obviousness of combining or modifying the primary reference to reach the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature‑by‑feature comparison for 102/103 questions
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 where there may be questions as to how limitations in the claims correspond to features in the prior art, the examiner, in addition to the requirements of (iii) and (iv), shall compare at least one of the rejected claims feature-by-feature with the prior art relied upon in the rejection. The comparison shall align the language of the claim side-by-side with a reference to the specific page or column, line number, drawing reference number and quotation from the reference, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide side-by-side alignment of claim language and exact prior art citations/quotations to show correspondence or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation for other rejections (non‑112/102/103)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection, other than those referred to in paragraphs (i) to (v), the examiner’s answer shall specifically explain the basis for the particular rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a specific, tailored explanation of the legal and factual bases for atypical or statutory rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of Patentability — General Explanation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The following findings of patentability, i.e., determinations of inapplicability of a proposed rejection, are applicable to the appealed claims. [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 explain each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection, or refer to the RAN if it clearly and completely sets forth the determination and complies with paragraphs (i)-(vi) (see below for statutory specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Inapplicability — 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph; the examiner’s answer shall explain how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is complied with, including, as appropriate, how the specification and drawings, if any, (a) do describe the subject matter defined by each of the claims proposed for rejection, and/or (b) would in fact enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter defined by each of the claims proposed for rejection without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain with specificity how the written description and enablement requirements are satisfied; address undue experimentation factors where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Inapplicability — 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph; the examiner’s answer shall explain how the claims do particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which “applicant” regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how claim language is definite and adequately delineates the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Inapplicability — 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection of the appealed claims under 35 U.S.C. 102; the examiner’s answer shall explain why the claims proposed for rejection are not anticipated and patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102, pointing out which limitations recited in the claims proposed for rejection are not found in the prior art relied upon in the proposed rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the missing limitations in the prior art and explain why those omissions render the proposal inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Inapplicability — 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection of the appealed claims under 35 U.S.C. 103; the examiner’s answer shall point out which limitations recited in the patentable claims are not found in the prior art relied upon in the proposed rejection, shall identify the difference between the patentable claims and the prior art relied upon by the third party requester and shall explain why the claimed subject matter is patentable over the prior art relied on by the third party requester. If the third party requester’s proposed rejection is based upon a combination of references, the examiner’s answer shall explain the rationale for not making the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which claim elements are absent from or not suggested by the prior art and why an asserted combination would not have been rationally made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature‑by‑feature comparison for third‑party proposed 102/103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each third party requester proposed rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 where there are questions as to how limitations in the claims define over features in the prior art even after the examiner complies with the requirements of (iii) and (iv), the examiner shall compare at least one of the claims proposed for rejection feature-by-feature with the prior art relied on in the proposed rejection. The comparison shall align the language of the claim side-by-side with a reference to the specific page or column, line number, drawing reference number, and quotation from the reference, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct side-by-side comparison and exact citations/quotations to resolve correspondence questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of Inapplicability — Other proposed rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection, other than those referred to in paragraphs (i) to (v), the examiner’s answer shall specifically explain why there is insufficient basis for making the particular proposed rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the specific factual/legal reasons demonstrating lack of basis for the proposed rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No New Ground of Rejection; No New Finding of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: This examiner’s answer does not contain any new ground of rejection. This examiner’s answer does not contain any new finding of patentability (i.e., no new determination of inapplicability of a proposed rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner’s answer may not include a new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.69(b)) or a new determination not to make a proposed rejection (37 CFR 41.69(c)). If a new ground or new determination is made, prosecution must be reopened (37 CFR 41.69(d)). This form paragraph must be included as a separate letter on a form PTOL‑90 (see MPEP §1209).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Argument — Examiner's Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with each of the contentions of appellants and respondents in their briefs with respect to the issues presented, and an explanation of the reasons for disagreement with any such contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any ground of rejection or inapplicability of proposed rejection is not argued and responded to by the appropriate party, the examiner shall point out each claim affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Proceeding(s) Appendix / Copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Proceeding(s) Appendix: copies of the court or Board decision(s) identified in the Related Appeals and Interferences section of this examiner’s answer are provided herein, or No decision rendered is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow form paragraph 26.61.01 (appendix), 26.61.02 (no related proceeding identified), or 26.61.03 (copies provided) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for Providing a Rebuttal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant(s) is/are given a period of ONE MONTH from the mailing date of this examiner’s answer within which to file a rebuttal brief in response to the examiner’s answer. Prosecution otherwise remains closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one‑month period may not be extended. The rebuttal brief must: (1) clearly identify each issue, and (2) point out where the issue was raised in the examiner’s answer and/or in the respondent brief. The rebuttal brief must be limited to issues raised in the examiner’s answer or respondent brief. No further submission (other than the rebuttal brief(s)) will be considered and will be treated per 37 CFR 1.939.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal Brief — Content Restrictions for Patent Owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief of the owner shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or an affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116 for amendments and evidence filed after final action but before or on the same date of filing an appeal and § 41.63 for amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing the appeal. The owner’s rebuttal may be directed to the examiner’s answer and/or any respondent brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal Brief — Content Restrictions for Requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief of any requester may be directed to the examiner’s answer and/or the respondent brief of the owner, but may not be directed to the respondent brief of any other requester. No new ground of rejection can be proposed by a requester. The rebuttal brief of a requester shall not include any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116(d) and § 41.63(c) for rules on affidavits/evidence filed after final action or after filing the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal Brief — Certification of Service
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief must include a certification that a copy of the rebuttal brief has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the proceeding. The names and addresses of the parties served must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to certify/service may be a reason for non‑compliance treatment under §41.71(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑compliant Rebuttal Briefs — Opportunity to Correct
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rebuttal brief is timely filed but does not comply with all requirements, appellant will be notified of reasons for non‑compliance and provided a non‑extendable period of one month to file an amended rebuttal brief. If the appellant does not file an amended rebuttal brief during the one‑month period, or files an amended brief that does not overcome all reasons for non‑compliance, that appellant’s rebuttal brief and any amended rebuttal brief will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry/refusal of rebuttal briefs is handled by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU); defective briefs receive notification letters and one chance to correct (one month non‑extendable).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Further Submission after Examiner's Answer
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner’s answer, only a rebuttal brief (or an amended rebuttal brief where one opportunity to correct a defective original rebuttal brief is given) will be received into the reexamination proceeding. No other submission will be considered, and any such other submission will be returned as an improper paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution remains closed except for the allowed rebuttal brief(s). See 37 CFR 1.939.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of Rebuttal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief filed [1] by [2] has been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a separate form paragraph 26.65 for each rebuttal brief received. In bracket 1 insert the date the rebuttal brief was filed; in bracket 2 insert the party that filed the rebuttal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Further Response / Forward to Board
rubrics_metrics.description: No further response by the examiner is appropriate. Any further reply/comments by any party will not be considered, and may be returned to the submitting party. The reexamination proceeding is being forwarded to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences for decision on the appeal(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.65.01 or 26.66.02 may be used to notify parties that proceeding is forwarded to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective Rebuttal Brief — Opportunity to Correct (Form 26.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rebuttal brief must (1) clearly identify each issue and (2) point out where the issue was raised in the examiner’s answer and/or in the respondent brief. In addition, the rebuttal brief must be limited to issues raised in the examiner’s answer or in the respondent brief. The rebuttal brief of Appellant [1] is defective because [2]. Appellant [3] is given ONE MONTH from mailing date to file an amended rebuttal brief; time may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amended rebuttal brief does not remedy the defect or raises a new one, appellant will be so notified and will not be given a second opportunity to file an amended rebuttal brief. Use form paragraph 26.66 once per appellant filing a defective original rebuttal brief; use 26.66.01 for defective amended rebuttal briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective Amended Rebuttal Brief — No Further Opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended rebuttal brief of Appellant [1] is defective because [2]. The original and amended rebuttal briefs have been placed in the file but will not be considered. There is no opportunity to file a second amended rebuttal brief, and any such submission will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph to notify appellant that the amended rebuttal brief is defective; follow with form paragraph 26.66.02 to forward to Board if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Hearing — When to Request and Fee/Timing Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when necessary or desirable. If desired, file as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' with the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer. The request must include a certification that a copy has been served in its entirety on all other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended. If no timely request and fee, the appeal will be assigned for decision on the briefs without an oral hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Hearing — Participation, Time Limits, Evidence/Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, oral argument will be limited to thirty minutes for each appellant or respondent who requested a hearing, and twenty minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. At the oral hearing, each appellant and respondent may only rely on evidence previously entered and present argument that has been relied upon in the briefs except as permitted for good cause (new argument based on recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner may only rely on argument/evidence relied upon in the answer except as permitted for good cause. The Board will determine order of arguments. No participation unless request filed and fee paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access to Reexamination Oral Hearings and Sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal involves reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless one of the appellants/respondents petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 that the hearing not be open, presents sufficient reasons, pays the petition fee, and the petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow petition procedures under 37 CFR 41.3 and pay fee set forth in 41.20(a) if requesting closed hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board Decision Content and Effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may affirm or reverse each decision of the examiner on all issues raised on each appealed claim, or remand the reexamination proceeding to the examiner for further consideration. The reversal of the examiner’s determination not to make a rejection proposed by a third party requester constitutes a decision adverse to the patentability of the claims and will be set forth in the decision as a new ground of rejection under paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmance of a rejection on any specified grounds constitutes a general affirmance of the examiner’s decision on that claim except as to any ground specifically reversed; remands and new grounds have specified procedural consequences.
